text:
alex_m: RFC follow-up — saw a liveness/race pattern in the merge/pack path that caused a tenant to starve for ~30s. want to capture root cause and next steps.

alex_m: short repro: noisy tenant A sends many small streaming requests. packer coalesces into windows, takes a lease, but prefetch + headroom signals sometimes revoke leases mid-pack. result: tenant B kept getting de-prioritized while A's unfinished batches held admission slots.

maya_w: :eyes: can you paste the lease/state sequence? was it lease revocation due to deadline miss or because headroom went negative?

alex_m: headroom dipped because prefetch loader pulled extra KV cache pages for A. packer had already committed logical slots. revocation came from the eviction thread when per-GPU headroom < config.batch_min_headroom.

jun_park: that matches the traces i saw. important detail: the revocation path clears the in-memory slot ledger but doesn't fully release the queue slice reference until coalesce finalizer runs, so admission thinks slots are in-use.

sarah-h: summary: two-phase release race — lease revocation marks slot free, but queue visibility lags -> double-booking prevention gates new admissions -> starvation for other tenants.

alex_m: exactly. my proposed short-term mitigations: 1) make revocation synchronous for small batches (fast path), 2) add a soft headroom buffer (configurable) so prefetch can't pull the gas pedal below X, 3) emit a metric `queue.slice_refcount` and `lease.pending_releases` for alerting.

maya_w: add to that: a short TTL on in-flight coalesce finalizer so if it stalls >100ms we forcibly detach and move to fallback. that buys us time for larger refactor.

jun_park: for the long-term, we should separate Admission (slot accounting + fairness) from Packing (coalesce + lease). current monolith mixes concerns. propose API: `Admission.acquire(tenant, tokens) -> AdmissionHandle` and `Packer.pack(handle, window) -> PackResult`. the handle would be immutable until released which guarantees visibility.

sarah-h: agree. immutability guarantees will simplify preemption: the revoker can mark handle.revoked = true and admission can immediately re-account without waiting for pack finalizer.

alex_m: here's a small pseudo-config i experimented with:
```yaml
runtime:
  headroom: 0.12              # percent of GPU memory reserved
  soft_headroom: 0.18         # prevent prefetch from starving packer
  coalesce_ttl_ms: 120        # fallback detach
  sync_revocation_threshold: 8 # number of slots under which revocation is synchronous
```

maya_w: nice. can we also incorporate per-tenant burst credits into Admission.acquire so an occasional burst doesn't evict others? maybe a token bucket per-tenant that admission consults before granting long-lived handles.

jun_park: yes — token-bucket + aging priority (recent throughput decays) should reduce long-tail tenant impacts. also we need to expose the per-tenant `pending_prefetch_bytes` in the console to diagnose these incidents.

sarah-h: observability items: instrument `lease.acquire_ms`, `lease.revoke_ms`, `pack.coalesce_ms`, `admission.waiters`, `queue.slice_refcount` and add an SLO alert: if `admission.waiters > 50` for >10s then escalate to oncall.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy to `staging/packers` scheduled at 04:00 UTC.

alex_m: plan for next week:
- implement soft_headroom + coalesce_ttl fast fallback (short-term patch)
- add queue & lease metrics to packer telemetry
- write Admission/Packer API proposal (long-term refactor) and run a small simulation harness to validate fairness rules

maya_w: i'll pick up the metrics and the coalesce_ttl fast-fallback patch. assigning myself.

jun_park: i'll draft the Admission/Packer API and a micro-sim harness (in go) to model headroom/preload interactions.

sarah-h: i'll add console panels and SLO alerts. also want a small postmortem doc template for this class of starvation incidents.

alex_m: thanks. action items captured. TL;DR: short-term guardrails (soft headroom + fast fallback + metrics) + long-term refactor to clear separation between admission and packing to avoid lease/visibility races.

maya_w: will post PRs and simulation plan later today.

jun_park: tagging @sre for visibility on SLO changes :cc @oncall

sarah-h: :thumbsup:

ops-bot: incident-bot: note created (id: 2026-IR-482) for follow-up and tracking.
